correctness.rationale: The permanent four-pebble invariant is sound. Remove the moved pebble and collapse duplicate anchors. With two distinct anchors a fresh point can be on or off their line. With three collinear anchors there is always an off-line point and there is a fresh on-line point exactly when q≥3. For a noncollinear triple the pair-lines meet only at the anchors, have q−1 further points each, and their union has 3q points in a plane of q²+q+1 points, so a point avoiding all three exists even at q=2. This works in an abstract plane as well as in the plane spanned by the triple in higher dimensions. The one-point case is unique. On a projective line C is universal; with at most three parked pebbles one can always match equality in line models of size at least four. The inequality, noncollinearity, four-distinct-points and four-collinear-points tests separate the five classes. With four named endpoints and one universally bound point, the claimed sentence really asserts skew lines; independent coordinate pairs give such lines for every d≥3, and plane lines always intersect. The four-pebble result gives exact minimality for matched order classes. Reconstructed from RESULT.md §§Assumptions and Proof. The inspected projective_profile_check.py and VERIFICATION.md describe representative prime-field checks, not a theorem for abstract planes or all dimensions; no uploaded code was run.
